title: BTC GAS-t decomposition — innovation vs GAS dynamics vs regime-switching
motivation: K1133 found BTC GAS-t reversal concentrated in P1 pre-institutional. GJR-Student-t also reverses in P1, hinting Student-t innovation — not GAS dynamics — is root cause. K1133 MS-GAS-t in-sample LRT all sig but no OOS. K1133b: (a) decompose via GAS-Normal baseline; (b) implement MS-GAS-t OOS with Klaassen (2002) state-prob recursion.

models.M4_GAS_N: GAS-Normal (NEW) — Creal-Koopman-Lucas Normal density, score = eps2 - 1 (Fisher-scaled log-variance form)
models.M5_GJR_N_std: GJR-N on shift-scale standardised returns (control for numeric-scaling artefact)
models.MS_GAS_t: 2-state Markov-switching GAS-t, OOS Klaassen (2002) state-prob recursion with per-state log-variance paths

methodology.lookahead_safety: Explicit assertion `train_start + len(train_data) == t_abs` at every refit. MS filter runs through train only; OOS forecast ξ_{t|t-1} = P ' ξ_{t-1|t-1} uses ONLY info up to prev obs.

references: Creal, Koopman, Lucas (2013) JASA 108:1-18 — GAS framework
Harvey (2013) Dynamic Models for Volatility & Heavy Tails

M4_GAS_N_vs_M3_GAS_t.interpretation: GAS-Normal vs GAS-t — isolates Student-t innovation contribution
GAS-Normal vs GAS-t — isolates Student-t innovation contribution

headline_conclusion: DECOMPOSITION: Student-t innovation is the root cause of BTC P1 reversal. GAS-Normal (no heavy-tail penalty) matches GJR-Normal. GAS dynamics per se are NOT the problem.
paper_implication: Mixed — full results needed for paper framing.
